Where is Hin Lad waterfall? | On Koh Samui's west side, 2–3 km inland from Nathon in Ang Thong subdistrict, at 9.5205, 99.9556. The trail starts beside the forest temple Wat Namtok Hin Lad, 5–10 minutes' drive from Nathon.
How long is the walk to Hin Lad? | The lowest tier is a few minutes from the trailhead, but walking between the lower and upper tiers takes 30–45 minutes each way on steep, uneven ground. Allow about two hours for the full walk and a swim.
Is there an entrance fee at Hin Lad waterfall? | No official fee is published. Visitors report a donation box at the trailhead; 20–50 THB is a reasonable contribution towards upkeep.
Can you swim at Hin Lad? | Yes, in the small, cool pools under the cascades, which are good for a dip after the climb. They are not deep enough for proper swimming or jumping, and they shrink from February to April.
Is Hin Lad better than Na Muang? | It is quieter and more of a forest walk, while Na Muang 1 has the bigger swimming pool and Na Muang 2 the taller falls. Choose Hin Lad if you are staying near Nathon or Lipa Noi; from Chaweng or Lamai, Na Muang is closer.
What should I wear at the Hin Lad temple? | Cover your shoulders and knees near the temple buildings, take your shoes off before entering any hall and keep voices low. A sarong over swimwear works well, with grippy closed shoes for the trail.
When is the best time to visit Hin Lad waterfall? | January, when the falls still flow well after the monsoon and the path has dried out, ideally between 08:00 and 10:00. October to December brings the most water but muddy, slippery paths; February to April the falls are low.
